title: Author the field-capability classification
description:
Author the classification document that assigns each field-capability surface to exactly one of four classes — algebraic law, algorithm, representation refinement, or kernel strategy — and names the canonical abstraction and cutover disposition for each.

## Background

gf2-core carries the FiniteField/ConstField hierarchy with the `Wide` delayed-reduction type and `#[doc(hidden)]` kernel hooks; gf2-algebra owns the frozen PackedField/PackedFieldVec lane abstraction; generic batch operations live in `crates/gf2-core/src/field/batch_ops.rs`; and selection state is spread across OnceLock function tables, per-field cached strategy pointers, the bit-buffer backend selector, and trait-associated threshold constants. The investigation linked from the epic's plan inventories these surfaces and their threshold constants with file:line citations. The classification decides, per capability: its class, its single canonical abstraction, which variants are superseded (with a cutover action or a named tracked exception), and which selection constants are tuning-profile-scoped versus algorithm-domain limits. The packed lane abstraction's gf2-algebra ownership is recorded with its boundary rationale rather than reopened.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A classification document in the epic's dev/active directory assigns each capability surface and each selection constant from the linked investigation to exactly one class, citing the defining code, and marks each constant profile-scoped or out of scope with a one-line reason.
- [hard] REQ-02: Each superseded or parallel variant carries an explicit cutover action or a named tracked exception, and the packed lane abstraction's ownership decision is recorded with rationale.

## Notes

- Grounding: dev/active/6dc81018-field-capability-dispatch/investigation.md (claim classifications, threshold inventory, consumer sweep).

planning.outcome: Capability surfaces and selection constants classified; canonical abstraction and cutover named per capability

terminal.consumer_family: Epic tasks that consume the classification document
terminal.test_boundary: Documentation review against the linked investigation
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Single design document synthesizing an already-cited investigation; no code changes

title: Retire the packed-trait parallel declarations in the research stub
description:
Retire the research stub's parallel PackedField/PackedFieldVec trait declarations so the production traits in gf2-algebra are the only live declaration in the tree.

## Background

`dev/research/packed_field_stub/` was the historical demonstration crate that proved the packed trait surface before production adoption; it redeclared `PackedField` and `PackedFieldVec` and carried stub `fold_mul` bodies that return zero. The production surface lives in `crates/gf2-algebra/src/packed/mod.rs`. The capability classification document records the cutover disposition for this variant; the planned action was archival under dev/archive with a pointer to the production home, preserving the original design-record linkage. Executed: the stub is archived at `dev/archive/packed_field_stub/`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The tree outside dev/archive contains exactly one declaration of the packed lane traits, in gf2-algebra.
- [hard] REQ-02: The stub's historical role and its design-record linkage remain discoverable from the archived location, and no document outside dev/archive refers to the stub as a live artifact.

planning.outcome: Research stub's parallel packed-trait declarations retired; production declaration unique outside dev/archive

terminal.consumer_family: Tree-wide resolution of the packed trait declaration
terminal.test_boundary: Tree search showing a single non-archive packed-trait declaration
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One bounded relocation plus a reference sweep bounded by the investigation's consumer list

title: Design the versioned tuning-profile format and selection integration
description:
Design the versioned tuning-profile artifact and how existing selection boundaries consume it.

## Background

Backend and crossover selection currently reads source constants, compile-time field shape, and runtime CPU features; no committed profile exists. The design fixes: the profile schema and its version field, the committed storage location, the loader API shape in gf2-core, the conservative default table and unknown-host fallback policy, and the calibration workflow as an explicit benchmark action under the repository's benchmark-lock conventions. The profile is data consumed at existing safe selection boundaries (OnceLock function tables, field constructors, algorithm-selector constants); it introduces no new crate dependency edges. Integration points are named for the pilot selector families designated by the classification; the schema carries an explicit extensibility rule for admitting further families in follow-on migrations.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A design document specifies the profile schema, versioning rule, committed storage location, and loader API, weighing at least two serialization/placement options before the recommendation.
- [hard] REQ-02: The document names the integration point for each pilot selector family designated by the classification, the conservative default and unknown-host fallback policy, and the explicit calibration workflow with its provenance fields.

planning.outcome: Tuning-profile schema, storage, loader API, defaults policy, and calibration workflow fixed by design

terminal.test_boundary: Documentation review of the design against the classification's profile-scoped selector families
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Single design document over an already-classified selector inventory; no code changes

title: Implement the tuning-profile type, loader, and conservative defaults
description:
Implement the tuning-profile data type, parser, and conservative default table in gf2-core per the profile design linked from the epic's plan.

## Background

The profile is a versioned, committed artifact; builds consume it deterministically. Unknown hosts and absent profiles select an embedded conservative default table backed by the tested scalar fallback paths. This issue delivers the mechanism only; existing selectors keep their current behavior until the cutover issue.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The loader parses the committed versioned profile and rejects malformed or unsupported-version input with explicit errors, with unit tests for both.
- [hard] REQ-02: An embedded conservative default profile is selected for unknown hosts or absent profiles, selection is deterministic for a fixed profile, and no existing selector changes behavior in this issue.

planning.outcome: Profile type, parser, and embedded conservative defaults land in gf2-core without selector behavior change

terminal.test_boundary: Unit tests over the loader's input-handling paths
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One new self-contained module against a fixed design; no consumer migration included

title: Implement the explicit host-calibration benchmark action
description:
Implement the calibration action that measures the pilot selector families on the current host and emits a versioned profile artifact.

## Background

Calibration is an explicit benchmark action under the repository's benchmark-mode and lock-wrapper conventions, never a build side effect. The emitted artifact records provenance — host, toolchain, git revision, and seeds — following the committed-receipt conventions, and must round-trip through the profile loader.

The harness lives as a benchmark target at `crates/gf2-core/benches/profile_calibration.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The calibration action runs only when explicitly invoked in benchmark mode and emits a profile artifact the loader accepts, with provenance fields populated.
- [hard] REQ-02: The calibration workflow is documented from invocation to committing the emitted profile, and a non-benchmark build shows no calibration side effect.

planning.outcome: Explicit calibration action emits a loader-valid, provenance-stamped host profile

terminal.consumer_family: Benchmark operators producing committed host profiles
terminal.test_boundary: Round-trip test: emitted artifact parses through the loader; explicit-invocation guard tested
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One harness over the already-implemented loader and a fixed measurement list

title: Pin the non-regression benchmark set and tolerance
description:
Pin the benchmark set, predeclared tolerance, and runnable procedure that gate the selector cutover.

## Background

A reconciled capability trait or migrated selector goes public only after a pinned benchmark set passes within a predeclared non-regression tolerance. The set covers the selector families marked profile-scoped for the pilot cutover; the tolerance is declared before any cutover measurement exists. This issue delivers the protocol and the runnable procedure only; baseline measurement is a separate issue.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed procedure names the pinned benchmarks covering the pilot selector families and states the non-regression tolerance, declared before any cutover measurement.
- [hard] REQ-02: The procedure executes end to end in benchmark mode on a prepared host, and is reproducible from its committed description alone.

planning.outcome: Pinned benchmark procedure and predeclared tolerance committed before any cutover measurement

terminal.test_boundary: Procedure executes end to end in benchmark mode
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Selecting an existing benchmark subset and declaring its tolerance; no measurement receipts

title: Record the pre-cutover baseline receipt
description:
Execute the pinned non-regression procedure before the pilot cutover and commit the baseline receipt.

## Background

The pinned procedure and its predeclared tolerance are already committed; this issue runs the procedure unmodified on the prepared benchmark host while the pilot selectors still read their pre-cutover constants, and commits the baseline receipt the later comparison is measured against.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A baseline receipt from the prepared benchmark host is committed with full provenance, produced by the pinned procedure unmodified.
- [hard] REQ-02: The receipt is consistent with the pinned procedure's protocol and reproducible from the procedure alone.

planning.outcome: Committed pre-cutover baseline receipt from the pinned procedure

terminal.consumer_family: Tasks comparing measurements against the pinned baseline
terminal.test_boundary: Receipt conformance to the pinned procedure
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One benchmark execution and one receipt against an existing procedure

title: Cut the bit-backend selector over to profile-driven selection
description:
Migrate the generic bit-buffer backend selector to read the tuning profile, with the current constant values as the embedded defaults.

## Background

The migrated selector family is `select_backend_for_size` and its threshold in `crates/gf2-core/src/kernels/backend.rs`, as marked profile-scoped by the capability classification. Under the default profile the selected values equal the current constants, so behavior is unchanged by construction; the scalar fallback paths stay reachable. Remaining profile-scoped constants migrate in follow-on work once the pilot receipt is recorded.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The selectors read their values from the loaded profile, and tests show selection equals the pre-cutover constants under the default profile.
- [hard] REQ-02: A non-default profile measurably changes the selected route in a test, and the scalar fallback path remains reachable and tested.

planning.outcome: Bit-backend selector consumes the profile; default-profile behavior identical by construction

terminal.test_boundary: Equivalence tests under the default profile; route-change test under a non-default profile; workspace CI
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One selector family in one crate with defaults preserving behavior

title: Record the post-cutover non-regression receipt
description:
Run the pinned non-regression procedure after the pilot cutover and commit the receipt showing the tolerance holds.

## Background

The pinned procedure and its predeclared tolerance exist before the cutover; this issue executes it on the prepared benchmark host after the pilot cutover lands and commits the receipt comparing against the baseline. The issue completes only once a receipt shows the tolerance holds. An excursion encountered on the way is preserved in the committed record together with its tracked rework, never overwritten.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed receipt compares post-cutover measurements against the baseline with full provenance and shows the predeclared tolerance holds for the pinned set.
- [hard] REQ-02: Any tolerance excursion encountered before the passing run is preserved in the committed record with its contradiction and tracked rework.

planning.outcome: Committed post-cutover receipt against the pinned baseline within the predeclared tolerance

terminal.test_boundary: Receipt conformance to the pinned procedure
terminal.worker_sized_reason: One benchmark execution and one receipt against an existing procedure

title: Spike Charon extraction of a trait-generic field algorithm
description:
Determine empirically whether Charon/Aeneas can extract a trait-generic gf2-core algorithm on the workspace MSRV, and record the outcome either way.

## Background

The current extraction covers concrete arithmetic only: the core invocation opaques `gf2_core::field`, and the prior attempt to extract generic `permanent_ryser<F>` was falsified — Charon did not monomorphise from a non-generic start root, and the direct extracted binding was descoped in favor of an abstract proof. The spike target is `batch_inverse<F: FiniteField>` (or a comparably small self-contained trait-generic gf2-core function). Vary the start roots and opaque list, including a generic start root and un-opaquing the field module for the target, and record every invocation and outcome. No proofs are authored in this issue; the proof sketch and proof implementation are planned in a follow-up round once this spike's outcome exists.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A spike record documents the exact Charon/Aeneas invocations attempted and their outcomes on the workspace MSRV toolchain.
- [hard] REQ-02: On success, the generated Lean for the generic target is preserved under the spike's extraction directory named in the record; on failure, the falsifying evidence is recorded and the required decision on the epic's extraction criterion is named for escalation.

## Notes

- Follow-on: a successful record triggers a follow-up planning round adding the approved-sketch and proof-implementation issues (sketch approved before proof code); a falsification escalates the epic's extraction criterion to the owner.

planning.outcome: Extraction feasibility of a trait-generic algorithm established with recorded evidence either way

terminal.test_boundary: Research review of the spike record; invocations reproducible from the record
terminal.worker_sized_reason: Bounded toolchain experiment on one small named target; no proof authoring

footprint.uncertainty: Local Charon invocation variants may be exercised outside scripts/verify-lean.sh without committing script changes
